A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DyCoke. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, latency and memory measurements, ablations and qualitative video examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a pruning-rate versus frame-count analysis and revised MVBench accuracy summaries.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the stated cache-update procedure. v1 describes exchanging KV/DP-cache tokens at each successive decoding step; v3 uses cosine similarity between attention distributions and updates only at low-similarity iterations. The temporal-merging procedure and overall two-stage architecture remain.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ActivityNet-QA, NextQA, PerceptionTest, VideoDetailCaption, VideoMME and MVBench. The new frame-count sweep uses retained VideoMME coverage; it changes experimental configurations rather than datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain full-token models, FastV with KV cache and LLaVA-PruMerge. The no-dynamic-pruning and random-pruning ablation controls also remain. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: v1 already evaluates 16- and 32-frame inputs. v3 Appendix D adds a joint sweep over 8, 16 and 32 frames and temporal-pruning K values from 0 to 1. The retained main experiments preserve their benchmarks, metrics, model sizes and stated settings.

E4.justification: Appendix D and new Figure 5 test how pruning sensitivity depends on input frame count. This supplements the unchanged token-selection, dynamic-pruning, over-pruning and attention-layer ablations in Table 5. Existing cost-effectiveness analyses and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: v1 Table 3 reports point accuracies. v3 adds ± quantities to all its accuracy entries, and Section 4.1 newly states that multiple MVBench experiments were averaged. Neither the run count, seeds nor the meaning of ± is specified; an explicit increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces several accuracies with revised averages: for 7B and 32 frames, DyCoke K=0.7 changes from 59.60 to 59.56±0.19, and full tokens from 58.79 to 58.81±0.14. Latency and memory values remain unchanged. Figure 5 adds pruning-sweep results; Tables 1, 2 and 4–8 retain their values.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and the FLOPs calculation retain their mathematical content. Equation 8 moves from Section 4.1 to Appendix C. Specifying the query-vector shape beside Equation 5 clarifies notation without introducing new mathematical reasoning, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the training-free temporal/spatial compression contribution, dynamic-pruning novelty claim and approximately 1.5× speedup and 1.4× memory-reduction claims. The added evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion explains frame-count sensitivity through redundancy and noise, distinguishes FLOPs from actual inference speed, and discusses Flash Attention compatibility. It also acknowledges possible information loss during rapid scene changes or critical temporal shifts and continuing obstacles to mobile deployment.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly identifies PyTorch as the implementation framework. GPU assignments, principal hyperparameters, evaluation tools, model dimensions and code-access information are retained. Relocating the FLOPs calculation does not add new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 adds eight cited works, including Mini-InternVL, the Llama3 quantization study and ST3. These mainly expand citation lists in the existing related-work discussion; the detailed positioning against prior token-compression approaches and the central novelty claim remain.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar and wording edits and updates affiliations. The main section structure remains, while the computing-cost discussion moves to Appendix C, new appendices D–E are inserted, and More Visualizations moves from Appendix C to F.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with clearer stage labels and revised token-flow graphics. v3 adds sensitivity Figure 5 and accommodates uncertainty values in Table 3. The existing appendix Figures 5–6 become Figures 6–7; most other displays and the two-column layout remain.

improvement.justification: v3 improves assessment of the method through MVBench uncertainty reporting, the frame-count/pruning sensitivity study, and explicit applicability limits in Appendix E. These are useful additions to largely unchanged evidence. The improvement remains limited because the uncertainty quantities and run count are undefined, and the revised cache-update trigger lacks a numerical similarity threshold.
